description: We are a tech-focused team passionate about AI, software, data, and interactive learning. For the Space Mission Design Game challenge, we want to turn real mission trade-offs like budget, mass, power, instruments, and orbital constraints into a fun, educational experience.
summary:
OrbitBridge: Mission Architect is an interactive educational satellite mission design and orbital operations sandbox built with Godot 4.7.2 and GDScript, playable in the browser (WebAssembly) and on Windows Desktop. Players step into the role of a mission architect: choosing from five Earth-observation and communications scenarios (Estuary Watch, Tropical Forest Watch, Polar Ice Survey, Communication, and Weather Monitoring) or creating a custom mission, assembling a spacecraft from real-inspired subsystem catalogs, passing engineering Flight Readiness checks, operating the satellite in 3D Earth orbit, and iterating on designs through controlled A/B comparison.

Understanding how power, mass, budget, orbit altitude, and ground-station contact windows trade off against one another is often locked behind complex aerospace tools. OrbitBridge bridges that gap with a hands-on, accessible simulation—supporting both English and Burmese (Myanmar)—so students and enthusiasts anywhere can experiment, learn from failure, and see why mission engineering decisions matter.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

OrbitBridge guides players through a complete six-stage mission engineering loop:

1. Mission Control: Launch a custom mission or select one of five prepared scenarios—Estuary Watch, Tropical Forest Watch, Polar Ice Survey, Communication, and Weather Monitoring.

2. Mission Creator: Configure mission objectives, target regions, observation/downlink goals, duration, and credit budget, supported by an illustrative orbital coverage preview.

3. Spacecraft Builder: Select bus, instrument, solar panels, battery, onboard storage, radio, launcher, launch profile, and orbit while inspecting the spacecraft in an interactive 3D preview.

4. Flight Readiness: Validate engineering constraints—including budget, CubeSat mass limits (such as the 1,330 g 1U CubeSat limit), launcher capacity, profile compatibility, target suitability, and power balance—before launch is permitted.

5. Mission Operations: Watch or manually operate the spacecraft in an interactive 3D Earth orbit view—capturing observations, transmitting data during ground contact windows, and saving power while tracking battery (Wh), storage, and simulation events.

6. Debrief & A/B Design Lab: Review calculated mission scores and goal explanations, save a completed flight as Design A, make a controlled change for Design B, and compare outcomes side-by-side.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

- Engine & Language: Godot Engine 4.7.2 (Compatibility renderer) and GDScript

- Platforms: Web (HTML5 / WebAssembly hosted on Netlify) and Windows Desktop (x86_64)

- Typography & Localization: English and Burmese (Myanmar) UI localization powered by bundled open-source Noto fonts (Noto Sans, Noto Sans Myanmar, Noto Sans Symbols, Noto Sans Math)

- Testing & Quality: Automated headless Godot validation, simulation, evaluation, and end-to-end UI/controller test suites

Benefits, Creativity & Factors Considered

- Learn-by-iterating Design Lab: Instead of a static quiz, players run controlled A/B experiments (e.g., upgrading a radio or battery) and immediately see the delta in returned data, lowest battery, mass, cost, and mission score.

- Accessibility & Inclusion: Runs completely client-side with no backend required, adapts to desktop and browser viewports, and supports Burmese (Myanmar) alongside English so non-native English learners can explore space systems engineering.

- Engineering Honesty: Clearly separates educational/illustrative visuals from deterministic simulation math, enforces strict Flight Readiness gates, and explains unmet goals transparently in Debrief.
